claims.text: Changing the percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr in HfNbTaTiZr HEA alters its mechanical properties.
Composition changes alter mechanical properties through variations in lattice distortion.
Composition changes alter mechanical properties through variations in atomic interactions.
The proposed intervention is to vary the percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
The composition-variation experiments should use a controlled environment and constant processing conditions.
Lattice distortion and atomic interactions are the structural mediators between composition and mechanical response.
Changes in lattice distortion and atomic interactions affect the alloy's mechanical behavior.
Changing elemental composition is predicted to alter strength.
Changing elemental composition is predicted to alter ductility.
Changing elemental composition is predicted to alter hardness.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr composition and its mechanical properties provide the baseline.
The relevant composition range is limited to variations that retain high-entropy-alloy characteristics.
There are insufficient data to specify the effects of varying each individual element on mechanical properties.
A systematic composition-variation study followed by mechanical-property characterization can test the hypothesis.
Tensile testing, hardness measurements, and microstructural analysis are proposed characterization methods.
The hypothesis is falsified if composition variations produce no significant changes in mechanical properties.
